newsitem.title: USA: Trump sues Atlantic City over road to rival casino.
newsitem.headline: Trump sues Atlantic City over road to rival casino.

text.p: Real estate magnate and casino owner Donald Trump has sued Atlantic City for agreeing to build a $330-million highway access road to a rival casino.
In papers filed Friday, Trump contended that the agreement to build a highway connector to the site of a proposed Mirage Resorts Inc. casino violates the state Constitution.

The deal negotiated between Mirage Chief Executive Stephen Wynn and Gov. Christie Whitman included $110 million from Mirage, $95 million from the state transportation trust fund and $60 million from the authority that operates the Atlantic City Expressway.
Trump's suit contends that another $65 million from the Casino Reinvestment Development Authority violates the state constitution, because its spending is supposed to benefit the elderly or disabled.

Wynn said the access road was a condition of his investing $750 million in a 2,000-room hotel-casino and retail and entertainment plaza on landfill in the city's Marina district. Two other gaming companies announced plans to join Wynn in building casino-hotels at the site.

Trump, long a rival of Wynn, also fought Atlantic City's gift of the landfill and a state initiative to repay Mirage for any cleanup costs. He has opposed the 2.2-mile viaduct and tunnel ever since it was announced last year.
Trump owns Altantic City properties through Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc.
